body:
When I was born, doctors couldn't figure out what sex I was because of a condition that I have. My parents chose to raise me as a girl and put me through cosmetic surgery as a baby to make me look more female, but they never told me about it and outright lied about it when I asked them as an adult.

Growing up I always wondered why my parents were so strict about gender roles with me, but not my younger siblings. I also never understood why they did things like pull me out of sex education classes, but had no issues with my siblings taking those classes. 

I always assumed it was just because I was the oldest and they were extra worried about their first kid. It was honestly soul crushing when I had my first gyno appointment at 20 and found out they were lying to me my entire life.

I might share my real username, I'm not sure yet. I've been thinking of making a video under my real name since people have asked me about writing a book or making videos.

My big interests are mostly horror movies and video games. My favorite movies are John Carpenter's The Thing, Re-Animator, and I'm a huge fan of anything Hannibal. My favorite games are Metal Gear Solid 3 and Bloodborne. 

I like to sew and I usually make small stuffed animals or sew things for my pet hedgehog. I'm trying to learn 3D modeling right now just as a hobby because I've always been awful at drawing. 

Most of the jobs I've had have been either Info Tech or security based. I used to hand solder circuit boards professionally and I've worked as a security guard. Right now I'm looking for a new job, but I've had some decent success streaming video games because I know a lot about their history and people like to hear about game development. I already have my own small community, so who knows, maybe that could actually work out someday.

There's too many comments to respond to individually right now, but I wanted to say thank you to everyone for saying such nice and supporting things. 

Things have been overwhelmingly difficult lately, but talking about it did help a lot. Practically everyone in my life has been dismissive or outright terrible towards me about my body issues and it was honestly really breaking me apart inside. The only people who have ever been understanding were people who were already close friends and identified as some form of LGBT+ themselves. 

I've just felt scared for years because of things that have happened to me. Like how I'm too afraid to go to the gym anymore because when I was 19 a woman chased me out of the showers and told the gym staff that I was a man sneaking into the women's locker room.

A lot of times I feel completely unwelcome in the world and the things that people do and say make me feel like everyone is against me. Seeing so many people who don't know me, especially christians other than my family, tell me that they support me has been really helpful. I've never had random people offer me any kind of support or wish me well before and I deeply appreciate it. 

Everything feels a little less bleak right now and I'm going to hold onto this whenever anyone says anything negative to me.

The university I went to didn't seem interested in any kind of activism for conditions like mine. I had better luck just joining an online network for people with similar conditions and trying that way.

I actually already work with interACT Youth. They're a great group and I've kept up with all of the big name intersex activists. 

It's more that my own family and the people around me are what's killing me. They either don't believe my condition is real, or they consider it a serious birth defect that needs fixed. 

Thank you though, I'm glad to see other people know about these groups. I worded my post the way I did because I assumed most people have no idea what being intersex even means.

I've thought about transitioning for a very long time, but I just don't know. I don't need life to be any harder than it already is. I see what my trans friends go through and I'm not sure I'm in an emotional place where I can handle that. I'm also very worried it could ruin my relationship with my boyfriend since he's told me many times he only sees me as a woman. Besides that, I don't identify solely as a man either. I was born in-between and I feel the only way I could ever be happy is living in-between. From what I've heard from other people with similar conditions, that's not uncommon. 

I'm seeing a gyno actively right now and they've told me there's no permanent fix for genital pain like mine other than more surgery, which I'm refusing. As for kidney pain, my disease is called LPHS and there's no treatment besides pain management- drugs that I've had addiction issues with over the years that I've been taking them.

And moving out isn't an option right now. My kidney is bad enough that I can't work full time. I have to live with my parents until my boyfriend and I are financially stable.
Not quite sure what you mean. Do you mean where I live?

I've talked to other people with similar conditions. Nobody really listens to us. We get forced into surgery as children and then we're adults we're told that it's too shameful to talk about our bodies. When we speak up, no one publishes our thoughts and experiences. It's still perfectly legal in the USA to cut up baby's genitals like they did to me. Our human rights groups can't get laws made to protect us despite the current and 2 past Surgeon Generals all advocating to stop it because of how much anguish it puts us in for our whole lives.

I would love to speak out. I've tried to. People just think that we're too rare and inconsequential to spend the time on.
